sourceClaims.section: Cable Specifications → Ethernet Cable Specifications → Maximum Cable Length
sourceClaims.supportedClaim: This hardware guide specifies a 100 m maximum Ethernet cable distance between the described router and connected equipment.
limitations: Product-specific illustration only. The game 100 m channel and inclusive comparator remain fictional; no universal limit for all copper or all Ethernet. No certification claim.

sourceClaims.section: Failures of the Five Wiremap Tests
sourceClaims.supportedClaim: Wiremap examines conductor continuity and termination; an open can reflect a broken conductor, poor connection or damaged connector.
limitations: The fixture supplies a diagnosed required-path break. An arbitrary open indication alone does not prove its location or cause; tester setup also matters.

sourceClaims.section: Chapter 5 Ethernet networks → Ethernet topologies → Repeater hubs; PDF page 101
sourceClaims.supportedClaim: Historical Ethernet repeater hubs receive and repeat data to linked segments with amplification and retiming; the described shared medium operates half duplex.
limitations: Not a modern wireless extender or a universal repeater topology allowance. Inability to restore an unchanged physical break is an explicit scenario inference, supported together with S04.

model.label: fictional-teaching-profile
model.scope: Exact reviewed profile projection. The introductory selector supplies T02 or T01 lengths; this profile checks length/continuity only. No full-link or branch success follows.
assumptions: Known compatible endpoints/media/terminations; one passive channel; supplied lengths exact and nonnegative.
Every required conductor is continuous unless explicitly broken; fresh tests required.
limitations: No cable certification, electromagnetic model, hidden permanent-link/patch-cord sublimits or real-product claim.
Repeater added without fixing a break cannot restore continuity. Regenerative topologies require separate reviewed segment limits and are unsupported here.

sourceClaims.supportedClaim: Physical entities transmit bits over physical media and can relay interconnected circuits; transmission may be synchronous or asynchronous.
limitations: Conceptual architecture only. No universal medium, numeric threshold, wire header, or claim that PHYs never have their own error mechanisms.

sourceClaims.supportedClaim: The Internet suite distinguishes application, transport, Internet and link functions; its grouping differs from the OSI teaching realms.
limitations: Historical architectural context, not current protocol configuration guidance; does not authorize seven invented mandatory headers.

sourceClaims.section: 2.1 Naming Conventions; Table 4 Linear and Gray Coding

limitations: T12 deliberately uses the declared linear toy labels. Do not substitute a real PHY map, count useful bitrate from symbol count, or imply the toy implements PAM4.
